# Sognefjorden Hiking Tours — Full Content

> Private Sognefjord hiking tours based in Høyanger, Norway. Four routes for all abilities — from easy waterfall walks to challenging alpine routes. Every tour is exclusively yours — your group, your guide, your pace.

Website: https://www.sognefjordenhikingtours.no/
Contact: post@sognefjordenhikingtours.no
Location: Høyanger, Sognefjord, Vestland county, Norway

---

## About Sognefjorden Hiking Tours

Sognefjorden Hiking Tours operates private Sognefjord hiking tours in Vestland county, Norway. The company is based in Høyanger, a small municipality on the Sognefjord — Norway's longest and deepest fjord, stretching 204 km inland from the coast and reaching depths of 1 308 m.

The surrounding mountains rise steeply from the fjord, creating one of Norway's most dramatic and accessible hiking landscapes. Trails climb from sea level through dense forest, past waterfalls, across open mountain terrain and into remote alpine wilderness — all within a short distance of the fjordside.

All tours are led by local expert guides with deep knowledge of the terrain, natural history, geology and cultural heritage of the area. Every booking is fully private: groups are never combined with strangers, and tours are tailored to the group's pace and ability on the day.

---

## Tours

### Fossestien — The Waterfall Path
- Difficulty: Easy
- Distance: 5–13 km (flexible — four starting points)
- Elevation gain: Up to 500 m (full circuit)
- Duration: 0.5–3 hours depending on section chosen
- Price: NOK 600 per person
- Suitable for: Families, children, beginners, first-time visitors, all fitness levels
- Season: Late May to September (shorter sections possible year-round)
- Page: https://www.sognefjordenhikingtours.no/fossestien/

Fossestien is one of Norway's most rewarding easy trails — a marked path along the Gaula River that threads past fourteen waterfalls and seven mountain lakes. The route follows historic trade paths used for centuries, connecting the valley communities of the Sognefjord region.

The trail is flexible by design: four parking areas allow you to pick the section that suits your group, whether that's a gentle one-hour valley stroll or the full 13 km mountain circuit. The path is clearly marked throughout with red F-signs and includes well-built bridges and boardwalks across the wettest sections.

In late spring the waterfalls run at full power from snowmelt, making for extraordinary sound and spectacle. In summer the mountain lakes are calm and perfect for a rest. This is the ideal introduction to the Sognefjord landscape for first-time visitors or families with younger children.

**Highlights:**
- Fourteen waterfalls along the Gaula River
- Seven mountain lakes — calm and beautiful in summer
- Historic trade route with centuries of local history
- Flexible length — choose 5, 8 or 13 km
- Bridges and boardwalks throughout — well maintained

**Good to know:**
- Suitable for most fitness levels — short sections possible for families with young children
- Trail marked with red F-signs from four parking areas
- Sturdy walking shoes recommended; hiking boots for the full circuit
- Best in late May–September; some boardwalks icy in winter

**Frequently asked questions:**
- Is Fossestien suitable for children? Yes — it is the most family-friendly hike in the area. The trail is well-marked, includes boardwalks, and can be as short as a one-hour valley walk.
- How long is the hike? Anywhere from 30 minutes to 3 hours, covering 5 to 13 km. Four parking areas let you choose the section on the day.
- What makes it special? Fourteen waterfalls and seven mountain lakes along a centuries-old trade route. In late spring the snowmelt waterfalls are at full power.
- What footwear is needed? Sturdy walking shoes for shorter sections; hiking boots with ankle support for the full 13 km circuit.

---

### Bergefjellet — Berg Mountain
- Difficulty: Moderate
- Distance: 7 km
- Elevation gain: 278 m
- Duration: 2.5–3 hours
- Price: NOK 900 per person
- Suitable for: Regular walkers, active visitors wanting a summit experience
- Season: Late May to September (possible in shoulder months with appropriate gear)
- Page: https://www.sognefjordenhikingtours.no/bergefjellet/

Bergefjellet is the Sognefjord region's signature half-day hike — a 7 km route that climbs from the Siplo ski centre area to a commanding summit with some of the finest views in all of Vestland. The initial section demands real effort, but the terrain opens up beautifully once the first cairn is reached.

From the summit the deep blue of the Sognefjord cuts between the mountains in every direction, with the broad sweep of Norway's longest and deepest fjord opening to the west. On clear days the Stølsheimen mountain massif fills the horizon to the south and east.

The marked trail continues from the summit across gently rolling terrain, offering the option to extend the walk or simply linger at the top with a packed lunch and the view.

**Highlights:**
- Panoramic views over the Sognefjord and surrounding peaks
- First cairn with dramatic views — the hard work done early
- Open, rolling terrain from the summit — option to extend the route
- Stølsheimen massif on the horizon
- Half-day circuit — back in time for lunch

**Good to know:**
- The initial section is the hardest part — take it steady
- Well-marked trail throughout; starts at Siplo skiing centre
- Hiking boots with ankle support recommended
- Bring a windproof layer — exposed at the summit

**Frequently asked questions:**
- How difficult is it? Moderate — the first section from Siplo is steep but the terrain opens up once the first cairn is reached. Regular walkers who are comfortable with a steady uphill will enjoy it.
- What can you see from the top? The full length of the Sognefjord stretches in both directions. On clear days the Stølsheimen massif fills the horizon to the south and east.
- Where does it start? At the Siplo ski centre area above the Sognefjord. Your guide confirms the exact meeting point at booking.
- How long does it take? 2.5 to 3 hours — most groups are back at the fjord before lunchtime.

---

### Kraftruta — The Power Route
- Difficulty: Hard
- Distance: 13.5 km
- Elevation gain: 700 m
- Duration: 4.5–5 hours
- Price: NOK 1 200 per person
- Suitable for: Fit, experienced hikers comfortable with sustained mountain effort
- Season: Late May to September only
- Page: https://www.sognefjordenhikingtours.no/kraftruta/

Kraftruta — "The Power Route" — is the Sognefjord region's most celebrated full-day hike. The trail climbs from the fjordside into the Berge mountains, following the infrastructure of the hydroelectric power network that shaped the area, before crossing the dramatic ridge between Toppenhytta and Skålebotn.

At 700 metres of climbing over 13.5 km, this is a serious mountain day that rewards with some of the finest views in the region. From the ridge, the full sweep of the Sognefjord opens beneath you — mountain upon mountain stretching in every direction, with the Stølsheimen wilderness to the south.

The route is well-marked throughout and can also be done as an overnight with a stay at Toppenhytta mountain hut.

**Highlights:**
- Magnificent Sognefjord panoramas from the ridge
- Unique industrial heritage — dam constructions and hydroelectric power infrastructure
- Full ridge traverse between Toppenhytta and Skålebotn
- Option to extend as an overnight at Toppenhytta
- Vestland's finest combination of nature and industrial history

**Good to know:**
- Solid hiking fitness essential — 700 m of sustained climbing
- Well-marked trail throughout; no technical scrambling
- Hiking boots with good ankle support required
- Carry food, water and full waterproof kit
- Weather can change fast on the ridge — guide will advise

**Frequently asked questions:**
- How hard is it? Hard. At 13.5 km with 700 m of elevation gain, it demands solid fitness and a full day of effort. No technical scrambling but sustained climbing throughout.
- What is the industrial heritage? The 'Power Route' name comes from the hydroelectric infrastructure built to harness mountain rivers for electricity — dams, water channels and engineering works from the 20th century.
- Where does it start and finish? Ridge traverse from Toppenhytta to Skålebotn. The guide arranges point-to-point logistics.
- Can I stay overnight? Yes — the route passes Toppenhytta mountain hut. Contact the operator for an overnight version.

---

### Solrenningen — Alpine Wilderness
- Difficulty: Very Hard
- Distance: 11.6 km
- Elevation gain: 890 m
- Duration: 4.5–5 hours
- Price: NOK 1 500 per person
- Suitable for: Experienced mountain hikers only — prior alpine experience required
- Season: Late May to September only — weather-dependent, may be cancelled in poor visibility
- Page: https://www.sognefjordenhikingtours.no/solrenningen/

Solrenningen is a remote alpine pasture at the heart of Stølsheimen — a vast protected landscape of some of western Norway's most dramatic high terrain. The route from Stølsdammen climbs nearly 900 metres into an area of traditional mountain farming that has been used for summer pasture for centuries.

This is a demanding route that requires good physical fitness and some previous mountain experience. The terrain becomes increasingly remote as you gain height, and route-finding beyond the waymarked sections requires attention. Your guide ensures safe navigation throughout.

**Highlights:**
- Stølsheimen protected landscape — one of western Norway's wildest areas
- Traditional mountain farming heritage at Solrenningen
- Alpine plateau with panoramic views across the massif
- True mountain wilderness — remote, quiet and spectacular

**Good to know:**
- Good fitness and prior mountain hiking experience required
- Some sections require careful navigation — guide essential
- Full mountain kit: waterproofs, warm layers, hiking boots, poles
- Carry emergency shelter, food and adequate water
- Weather-dependent — not suitable in poor visibility

**Frequently asked questions:**
- What is Stølsheimen? A protected landscape in western Norway — vast mountain wilderness of broad plateaus, deep valleys and ancient summer farming traditions. Largely untouched and rarely visited by tourists.
- How difficult is it? Very Hard. At 11.6 km with 890 m of elevation gain into remote alpine terrain, it requires good fitness and previous mountain experience.
- What experience do I need? You should be comfortable with full mountain days and have previous experience in exposed or remote terrain. Kraftruta is a good prerequisite.
- Is it safe? With a qualified guide, yes. Tours are weather-dependent — if visibility is poor or conditions are unsafe, the tour is rescheduled.

## Practical Information

- **Booking:** https://www.sognefjordenhikingtours.no/#book — submit an enquiry form and receive confirmation within 24 hours
- **What's included:** Qualified local guide for the full hike, route planning, safety equipment
- **What's not included:** Transport to Høyanger, personal hiking gear, food and water, travel insurance
- **Cancellation:** Free cancellation up to 48 hours before the tour
- **Group size:** All group sizes accepted — all tours are private, no minimum group size
- **Languages:** English-guided tours
- **Getting there:** Høyanger is approximately 3 hours from Bergen by road and ferry via the E16 and fjord ferry crossings. Also accessible via the Nærøyfjord ferry network from Flåm.
- **When to visit:** Main season late May to September. Late May–June for spectacular waterfalls. July–August for warmest, most settled conditions.
